course.Title: JavaScript Introduction
course.description: JavaScript is a programming language that makes web pages interactive. It runs in browsers and can also run on servers.
course.exampleCode:
<!-- Inline JavaScript -->
<button onclick="alert('Hello!')">Click me</button>

<!-- Internal JavaScript -->
<script>
  console.log('Hello, World!');
  var name = 'Alice';
  alert('Welcome, ' + name);
</script>

<!-- External JavaScript -->
<script src="app.js"></script>

course.Title: JavaScript Syntax
course.description: JavaScript syntax defines how JavaScript code is written and executed.

course.Title: JavaScript Statements
course.description: Statements are executable instructions that perform actions.

course.Title: JavaScript Comments
course.description: Comments explain code and are ignored by JavaScript engines.

course.Title: JavaScript Variables
course.description: Variables store data values. Use var or var (avoid var).

course.Title: JavaScript Data Types
course.description: Data types define what kind of data a variable can hold.

course.Title: JavaScript Operators
course.description: Operators perform operations on variables and values.
course.exampleCode:
// Arithmetic
var sum = 10 + 5;   // 15
var diff = 10 - 5;  // 5
var product = 10 * 5; // 50
var quotient = 10 / 5; // 2
var remainder = 10 % 3; // 1
var power = 2 ** 3; // 8

// Comparison
10 > 5;      // true
10 < 5;      // false
10 == 10;    // true
10 === '10'; // false (strict)

// Logical
true && false;  // false
true || false;  // true
!true;          // false

course.Title: JavaScript String Methods
course.description: Strings have built-in methods for manipulation.
course.exampleCode:
var text = 'Hello World';

text.length;              // 11
text.toUpperCase();       // 'HELLO WORLD'
text.toLowerCase();       // 'hello world'
text.indexOf('World');    // 6
text.slice(0, 5);         // 'Hello'
text.substring(0, 5);     // 'Hello'
text.replace('World', 'JavaScript');
text.split(' ');          // ['Hello', 'World']
text.trim();              // removes whitespace
text.includes('World');   // true
text.startsWith('Hello'); // true
text.endsWith('World');   // true

course.Title: JavaScript Template Literals
course.description: Template literals use backticks and allow string interpolation.

course.Title: JavaScript Numbers
course.description: Numbers can be integers, decimals, or special values like Infinity and NaN.

course.Title: JavaScript Math Object
course.description: The Math object provides mathematical functions and constants.
course.exampleCode:
// Constants
Math.PI;        // 3.14159...
Math.E;         // 2.71828...

// Methods
Math.abs(-5);           // 5
Math.round(4.6);        // 5
Math.floor(4.9);        // 4
Math.ceil(4.1);         // 5
Math.pow(2, 3);         // 8
Math.sqrt(16);          // 4
Math.max(3, 7, 2);      // 7
Math.min(3, 7, 2);      // 2
Math.random();          // 0 to 1
Math.sin(Math.PI / 2);  // 1
Math.cos(0);            // 1
